you want to go into other rooms or open: you receive a present by post from a relative
stay in the rooms you are invited into: phone, message or write to say thank you soon
other rooms are private: the giver wants to know it arrived and that you liked it

you want to go into other rooms or open: you want to tell your parent something while they talk to someone
stay in the rooms you are invited into: wait for a pause, or put your hand gently on their arm and wait
other rooms are private: interrupting is rude, but they know you are waiting

you want to go into other rooms or open: you are in a place of worship during a service
stay in the rooms you are invited into: sit quietly, stand or sit when others do if you are comfortable, and do not take photos unless allowed
other rooms are private: it shows respect for the worship

you want to go into other rooms or open: you go to a museum or art gallery
stay in the rooms you are invited into: do not touch exhibits unless signs say you can, and walk calmly
other rooms are private: exhibits can be fragile and old

you want to go into other rooms or open: you get a compliment and then show off about it
stay in the rooms you are invited into: say thank you and leave it there

you want to go into other rooms or open: a classmate is autistic and does not like loud noise or changes
stay in the rooms you are invited into: be patient, keep calm and respect their needs
other rooms are private: autistic people experience the world differently

you want to go into other rooms or open: a classmate has ADHD and finds it hard to sit still
stay in the rooms you are invited into: be kind and do not call them naughty
other rooms are private: it is a difference in how the brain works, not bad behaviour

you want to go into other rooms or open: someone has a disability you cannot see, like diabetes or a heart problem
stay in the rooms you are invited into: believe them when they say they need something, like a snack or a rest
